sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Hindsight is a memory system for AI agents. It stores what an agent learns, recalls the relevant memories later and can reflect on them, so agents improve over time instead of forgetting everything between conversations.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agents usually lose context between sessions, and plain RAG or knowledge graphs only recall text. Hindsight extracts facts, entities, relationships and time information from what you store, and the README reports state-of-the-art results on the LongMemEval benchmark.
whoFor: Developers building agents that need long-term memory
Teams adding memory to chatbots and assistants
Coding agent users who want persistent memory
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a self-hostable memory layer with SDKs, an MCP server and a two-line LLM wrapper. A hosted Hindsight Cloud is also available.
requirements: An API key for an LLM provider, or a local model through Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp

overview: Hindsight runs as a server with an API on port 8888 and a UI on port 9999. Memories live in banks. You interact through three operations: retain stores information, recall searches memories (including by time), and reflect generates a response that takes the stored memories into account.

Behind the scenes, retain uses an LLM to extract key facts, temporal data, entities and relationships and normalises them into a searchable form. It works with 25+ LLM providers through HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Bedrock and local models.

There are clients for Python, Node.js and Go, a CLI, an MCP server exposing retain, recall and reflect as tools, and an LLM wrapper that adds memory to existing OpenAI or Anthropic calls automatically. You can also embed it in Python with no separate server. It is MIT licensed.

steps.title: Start Hindsight
steps.body: API on http://localhost:8888, UI on http://localhost:9999.
steps.code:
docker run -it --pull always --name hindsight --restart unless-stopped -p 8888:8888 -p 9999:9999 \
  -e HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_API_KEY=$OPENAI_API_KEY \
  -v hindsight-data:/home/hindsight/.pg0 \
  ghcr.io/vectorize-io/hindsight:latest

steps.title: Install and start the API
steps.code:
pip install hindsight-api
export HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_API_KEY=sk-xxx
hindsight-api

steps.title: Install with Helm
steps.code:
helm install hindsight oci://ghcr.io/vectorize-io/charts/hindsight \
  --set api.llm.provider=openai \
  --set api.llm.apiKey=sk-xxx \
  --set postgresql.enabled=true

environment.name: HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_API_KEY
environment.description: API key for the LLM provider Hindsight uses to extract memories.

environment.name: HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER
environment.description: Which LLM provider to use, for example openai, anthropic, gemini or ollama.

environment.name: HINDSIGHT_DB_PASSWORD
environment.description: Database password when using the external PostgreSQL docker compose setup.

tutorial.title: Store and recall your first memories
tutorial.useCase: Use the Python client to retain a fact, recall it and reflect on it.

steps.title: Connect and retain a memory
steps.code:
from hindsight_client import Hindsight

client = Hindsight(base_url="http://localhost:8888")
client.retain(bank_id="my-bank", content="Alice works at Google as a software engineer")

tutorial.expected: Recall returns the stored memory about Alice, and reflect generates a response based on what the bank knows.

troubleshooting.problem: Bare-metal install problems on an Intel Mac
troubleshooting.solution: Use hindsight-all-slim, as the README says.

troubleshooting.problem: Want to use a local model
troubleshooting.solution: Set HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_PROVIDER to ollama, lmstudio or llamacpp.
